summary.intent: Bootstrap the newly-configured release-please system (Phase 41), align api-client versions with the API, expose the API version on the /health endpoint, and fix various CI/CD issues that emerged during the first real use of the release pipeline.
summary.outcome: Bootstrap tags created to fix excessive PR #427 changelog, api-client packages aligned to v0.35.0, health endpoint now returns version field, post-merge workflow replaced with pre-merge PR branch injection, merge commit filtering added to release preview, and openapi.json extra-files misconfiguration fixed. PR #430 release gate still blocked at session end due to openapi.json version comparison issue.

repo: Release-please treats the entire commit history as unreleased when no prior tags exist — bootstrap tags must be created at the pre-phase commit SHA to establish a starting point
The health endpoint is manually defined in generate-openapi.ts (not via HealthController) because TypeORM dependency prevents controller instantiation in the script context

openapi.json is a generated file under packages/api-client/ — it should not be managed by release-please extra-files because release-please reformats the entire JSON (~700 line diff) instead of doing a surgical version bump

release-please extra-files jsonpath config resolves paths relative to the package directory — packages/api-client/openapi.json listed under apps/api resolved to the nonexistent apps/api/packages/api-client/openapi.json
The PR release preview script processed merge commits as conventional commits, causing false release labels across unrelated packages whenever a branch was merged before the PR
commit message type matters for release-please bump logic: fix: triggers patch bump and adds release labels; chore(ci): is the correct type for CI-only changes that should not trigger version bumps
npm_package_version env var is unreliable for reading package version — must read package.json explicitly via fs.readFileSync with a fallback
Branch protection rules (legacy UI) lack per-actor bypass; the newer Rulesets UI supports bypass actors but has had stability issues on this repo

code.finding: Version reading moved to shared src/version.ts module; originally used npm_package_version which is unreliable, now reads package.json via readFileSync with __dirname resolution
Health endpoint now returns version field sourced from shared API_VERSION constant in src/version.ts

Health endpoint is manually spec-defined here (not auto-generated from controller) due to TypeORM dependency preventing controller instantiation; version field and error/details fields added to the manual schema
Merge commits (2+ parents) must be filtered before conventional commit parsing to prevent false release labels from version bump merge commits
Manual override labels (existing higher-or-equal release label) must feed back into packageBumps map so release-as derivation uses the reconciled bump level, not the computed lower level

release-as injection must: (1) snapshot base branch config to avoid clearing entries from prior merged PRs, (2) never downgrade an existing release-as to a lower bump, (3) apply bump-minor-pre-major logic for 0.x packages on breaking changes
Concurrency group per PR number prevents overlapping runs; fork guard on commit step prevents forks from pushing back to origin
OpenAPI spec comparison must exclude info.version field — the version is dynamic from package.json and release-please does not reliably update it in the generated spec

workflow: When release-please has no prior tags, bootstrap by creating tags at the last known stable commit SHA and pushing them — the next workflow run will regenerate the release PR with only commits since those tags

The post-merge workflow pattern (push release-as to main after merge) breaks with branch protection; pre-merge injection (compute and commit release-as targets onto the feature branch before it merges) is the correct architecture
Squashing a PR with the wrong commit prefix (fix: instead of chore:) propagates through release-please and adds unintended version bump labels — always verify commit message type before force-pushing
When resolving stale git index.lock, remove the file manually: rm .git/index.lock, then retry the git operation
Generated files should be excluded from release-please extra-files management; version comparison in CI should normalize away version fields that are dynamically derived at generation time

friction: Branch protection blocked the post-merge release workflow from pushing release-as config to main — required a full architecture change from post-merge push to pre-merge PR branch injection
release-please extra-files jsonpath reformatted the entire openapi.json (~700 lines) instead of doing a surgical version field update, causing the CI spec comparison to fail
Stale .git/index.lock from a background process blocked branch switching
fix: commit message on a CI-only change accidentally triggered version bump labels across multiple packages — required squash/force-push to correct

Extra-files path in release-please-config.json was resolved relative to the package directory (apps/api/), making packages/api-client/openapi.json resolve to a nonexistent path — took three PR iterations to diagnose and fix
Release-please PR #430 required multiple rerun cycles because fixes landed in separate PRs that each triggered a re-evaluation
npm_package_version was unreliable in the OpenAPI generation context, requiring a switch to explicit fs.readFileSync — flagged by automated reviewers
open_items: PR #430 (release PR for v0.36.0) still has failing Verify API Spec & Client check at session end — fix is in-flight via openapi.json version exclusion from CI comparison
Versioning strategy for web and desktop apps: discussion log says monotonic (major.minor) but semver was implemented; user deferred with 'semver is fine for now'
openapi.json should have release-please extra-files entry removed (done) and CI check should exclude info.version from semantic comparison (in-flight at session end)
Bootstrap tags were created but release PR #430 still needs to be merged to complete the first real release cycle end-to-end verification
